elements.element: No non-compete restriction applies to Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 states that nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service and expressly acknowledges that Customer made no non-compete commitment. The revised Section 12.4 permits Customer to develop, market, sell, or acquire competing products or services.

elements.element: No field-of-use restriction applies to Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly permits Customer to conduct business in any field or territory, and the revised Section 12.4 permits competition in any territory.

elements.element: Any restriction is limited to one competing product.
elements.evidence: No non-compete restriction remains, so the condition requiring this scope limitation is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: The competing product subject to any restriction is expressly named.
elements.evidence: No product is subject to a non-compete restriction; therefore, the conditional naming requirement is not triggered.

elements.element: Any restriction applies only during the term.
elements.evidence: No non-compete restriction remains. The reference to the term and the following twenty-four months modifies an affirmative permission, not a restriction.

elements.element: Any restriction is capped at 12 months.
elements.evidence: No non-compete restriction remains, so there is no restricted period exceeding 12 months.

elements.element: Any restriction includes a carve-out for Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly permits Customer to develop any product or service, and revised Section 12.4 also permits development of competing products or services.

elements.element: Any restriction includes a carve-out for Customer's acquisitions.
elements.evidence: Sections 12.3 and revised 12.4 expressly permit Customer to acquire products or services, including competing ones.

result.reason: The operative language reaches the preferred position by converting the non-compete prohibition into permission while retaining Section 12.3's comprehensive no-restriction language. Because no non-compete remains, the fallback limitations are also satisfied, with development and acquisition additionally protected expressly. The change is substantively targeted and leaves the unrelated employee restriction unchanged. Drafting quality is reduced by duplicate Section 12.4 numbering and by retaining a twenty-four-month temporal phrase in an affirmative permission, which is unnecessary and could create avoidable negative-implication ambiguity despite Section 12.3's broader protection.
